senses.title: The number between seven and nine
senses.definition: the number between seven and nine, written 8
senses.definitionCN: 七和九之间的数目，写作 8
senses.example: Eight children stood in a row on the playground.
senses.exampleCN: 八个孩子在操场上站成一排。
senses.why: Eight goes back to Old English eahta and shares its root with Latin octo, both from the same Indo-European word for eight.
senses.whyCN: eight 来自古英语 eahta，与拉丁语 octo 同源，都出自印欧语里表示「八」的那个词。

senses.title: A group of eight people or things
senses.definition: a group made up of exactly eight people or things
senses.definitionCN: 恰好由八个组成的一组
senses.example: The eight of us shared one taxi.
senses.exampleCN: 我们八个人共乘一辆出租车。
senses.why: Once the count is fixed, the number can stand alone for the group that has exactly that many, so eight becomes a noun.
senses.whyCN: 数目一旦确定，数词就能单独指「恰好有这么多人的那一群」，eight 于是当名词用。

senses.title: Eight o'clock
senses.definition: the hour of eight on a clock
senses.definitionCN: 钟面上的八点整
senses.example: The train leaves at eight.
senses.why: A clock face repeats the numbers twice a day, so the hour itself is simply called by its number, giving the time sense of eight.
senses.whyCN: 钟面一天转两圈，每个数字都对应一个整点，所以那个时刻直接用数词称呼，eight 因此也表示八点。

senses.title: The part of the day between afternoon and night
senses.definition: the time between the end of the afternoon and night
senses.definitionCN: 下午结束到入夜之间的那段时间
senses.example: The evening air was cool after the rain.
senses.why: Evening comes from Old English ǣfnung, 'the approach of night', from ǣfen, the word for the fading end of day.
senses.whyCN: evening 来自古英语 ǣfnung「夜色临近」，词根 ǣfen 指白昼渐渐暗下去的那一段。

senses.title: A social event held in the evening
senses.definition: an occasion or performance that takes place in the evening
senses.definitionCN: 在傍晚或晚上举行的活动、演出
senses.example: We attended a musical evening at school.
senses.exampleCN: 我们参加了学校的一场音乐晚会。
senses.why: Because gatherings are usually held at that hour, the time word came to name the gathering itself, as in a musical evening.
senses.whyCN: 聚会通常放在这个时段，于是这个表示时间的词也用来称呼聚会本身，如 a musical evening。

definition_en: the organ of sight, or to look at something closely
core_image: 一只睁开的眼睛，瞳孔里映着窗外的光
scene: 清晨的光照进房间，她的眼睛映着窗外的树影。She opened her eyes and saw the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 eye 是「眼睛」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她睁开眼睛看见了太阳。

pos.zh: 名词：眼睛、眼光、针眼、风暴中心

senses.title: The organ of sight
senses.definition: the part of the body with which a person or animal sees
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物用来看东西的器官
senses.example: She opened her eyes and saw the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 她睁开眼睛看见了太阳。
senses.why: Eye goes back to Old English ēage, related to German Auge, and names the organ that takes in light.
senses.whyCN: eye 来自古英语 ēage，与德语 Auge 同源，指接收光线的器官。

senses.title: The ability to notice or judge
senses.definition: the ability to notice or judge something well
senses.definitionCN: 看出好坏、察觉细节的能力
senses.example: She has an eye for colour.
senses.why: A good eye catches what others miss, so the organ's name transferred to the skill of noticing and judging.
senses.whyCN: 好眼力能看见别人漏掉的东西，于是这个器官的名字转到了「察觉与判断」的能力上。

senses.title: A small hole or centre shaped like an eye
senses.definition: a small hole or central space, as in a needle or a storm
senses.definitionCN: 针上的小孔，或风暴中心那样的圆形区域
senses.example: The thread went through the eye of the needle.
senses.why: A needle's hole and a storm's calm centre are round openings like a pupil, so eye names these small centres too.
senses.whyCN: 针上的孔和风暴中心都是像瞳孔一样的圆形开口，于是 eye 也指这类中心。

senses.title: To look at something closely
senses.definition: to look at something closely, often with interest or suspicion
senses.definitionCN: 仔细看某物，常带兴趣或戒备
senses.example: He eyed the cake on the table.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so to eye something is to fix one's eyes on it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，eye 某物就是把眼睛盯在它上面。

definition_en: the front of the head, or to confront something

senses.title: The front of the head
senses.definition: the front part of the head, from the forehead to the chin
senses.definitionCN: 头部从额头到下巴的正面
senses.example: She washed her face with cold water.
senses.why: Face came from Old French face, from Latin facies, 'form, appearance', and it names the front of the head.
senses.whyCN: face 来自古法语 face，源头是拉丁语 facies「外形、面貌」，指头部的正面。

senses.title: The expression shown on the face
senses.definition: the look or expression that a person shows
senses.definitionCN: 一个人脸上流露的神情
senses.example: His face showed that he was pleased.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上显出满意的神色。
senses.why: Because feelings appear on the front of the head, the word for that surface also names the expression it carries.
senses.whyCN: 情绪总是显现在头部正面，所以这个表示正面部位的词也指它带有的神情。

senses.title: A front or outer surface
senses.definition: the front or outer surface of an object
senses.definitionCN: 物体朝向外面的一面
senses.example: The face of the cliff was wet with rain.
senses.exampleCN: 悬崖的岩面被雨打湿了。
senses.why: Anything with a front side has a face the way a head does, so the word extends to walls, clocks and cliffs.
senses.whyCN: 任何有正面的事物都像头一样有「脸」，于是这个词扩展到墙面、钟面和崖面。

senses.title: Standing or dignity in others' eyes
senses.definition: the respect or good opinion one has in front of others
senses.definitionCN: 在别人眼里的体面与尊严
senses.example: He lied to save face.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了保全面子撒了谎。
senses.why: The face is what others see, so losing face means losing the good appearance one presents to people.
senses.whyCN: 脸是别人看见的部分，所以 lose face 就是丢掉呈现在众人面前的好样子。

senses.title: To confront or deal with something
senses.definition: to confront a person or thing, or to be turned toward it
senses.definitionCN: 迎面应对某人某物，或朝向它
senses.example: He had to face the truth.
senses.why: To face something is to put your face toward it, so the noun became a verb of confronting or being turned toward.
senses.whyCN: face 某物就是把脸转向它，于是名词转作动词，表示面对或朝向。

senses.definitionCN: 某些教会中对神职人员的称呼
senses.example: Father Brown will say the morning service.
senses.why: A priest is addressed as Father because the congregation is seen as a family that he guides like a parent.
senses.whyCN: 信徒把会众看作一个家庭，神职人员像父辈一样引导他们，所以被称作 Father。

senses.title: The founder or originator of something

definition_en: an animal that lives in water, or to catch or search for something
core_image: 一条银色的鱼在水草间摆尾，鳞片反着水光
scene: 池塘里一条银色的鱼从水草间游过。We caught a fish in the river.
sceneCN: 这里 fish 是「鱼」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们在河里钓到了一条鱼。

derivatives.zh: 由 fisher 与 man 复合，义为「渔民」
由 fish 加 -ing 构成，义为「钓鱼」
由 fish 加 -y 构成，义为「可疑的」
由 fish 加 -ery 构成，义为「渔场」

senses.title: An animal that lives in water
senses.definition: a cold-blooded animal that lives in water and breathes through gills
senses.definitionCN: 生活在水里、用鳃呼吸的冷血动物
senses.example: We caught a fish in the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河里钓到了一条鱼。
senses.why: Fish goes back to Old English fisc and shares its root with Latin piscis, the word for the water animal.
senses.whyCN: fish 来自古英语 fisc，与拉丁语 piscis 同源，指这种水生动物。

senses.title: The flesh of fish eaten as food
senses.definition: the flesh of fish used as food
senses.definitionCN: 供食用的鱼的肉
senses.example: We had fish and chips by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海边吃了炸鱼薯条。
senses.why: Once the catch reaches the table it is food rather than a living creature, so fish also names the flesh on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 捕上来的鱼端上餐桌后就是食物而不是活物，所以 fish 也指盘里的鱼肉。

senses.title: To catch fish
senses.definition: to try to catch fish
senses.definitionCN: 设法捕到鱼
senses.example: They fished in the lake all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在湖里钓了一上午鱼。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so fish names the work of catching fish.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，fish 表示捕鱼这个动作。

senses.title: To search for something in a roundabout way
senses.definition: to try to get information or praise indirectly
senses.definitionCN: 不直说，绕弯子套取信息或称赞
senses.example: She fished for praise after the talk.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲之后她拐着弯想讨称赞。
senses.why: Fishing means reaching into water and hoping something comes up, and that picture fits reaching for a hidden answer or compliment.
senses.whyCN: 捕鱼是把网伸进水里、盼着有东西上来，这个画面正合「伸手去够」藏着的回答或好话。

definition_en: the number 5, or a group of that size

scene: 桌上有五颗玻璃弹珠，排成一个小圈。Five children sat at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 five 是「数字五」（第 01 个义项）；句意是五个孩子坐在桌边。

senses.title: The number between four and six
senses.definition: the number between four and six, written 5
senses.definitionCN: 四和六之间的数目，写作 5
senses.example: Five children sat at the table.
senses.why: Five goes back to Old English fīf and is related to German fünf and Latin quinque, all from one Indo-European word.
senses.whyCN: five 来自古英语 fīf，与德语 fünf、拉丁语 quinque 同源，都出自同一个印欧语词。

senses.title: A group of five people or things
senses.definition: a group made up of exactly five people or things
senses.definitionCN: 恰好由五个组成的一组
senses.example: The five of us walked home together.
senses.exampleCN: 我们五个人一起走回家。
senses.why: A fixed count can stand for the set it counts, so five works as a noun for a group of exactly that size.
senses.whyCN: 固定的数目可以代替它所数的集合，所以 five 能当名词，指恰好五个的一群。

senses.title: Five o'clock
senses.definition: the hour of five on a clock
senses.definitionCN: 钟面上的五点整
senses.example: We meet at five.
senses.why: The hour on a clock carries the same number, so five also names five o'clock in everyday arrangements.
senses.whyCN: 钟面上的整点也带着同一个数字，所以 five 在日常约定里也表示五点。

definition_en: the coloured part of a plant, or to produce flowers
core_image: 一朵刚开的红花立在绿叶间，花瓣上还挂着露水
scene: 窗台上的一盆花开了，红色花瓣上挂着露水。A red flower opened on the balcony.
sceneCN: 这里 flower 是「花」（第 01 个义项）；句意是阳台上开了一朵红花。

derivatives.zh: 由 flower 与 pot 复合，义为「花盆」
由 flower 加 -ing 构成，义为「开花的」
由 flower 与 bed 复合，义为「花坛」

senses.title: The coloured part of a plant
senses.definition: the part of a plant that carries the petals and makes seeds
senses.definitionCN: 植物上长花瓣、结种子的部分
senses.example: A red flower opened on the balcony.
senses.why: Flower came from Old French flour, from Latin flos, 'flower', and names the blooming part of a plant.
senses.whyCN: flower 来自古法语 flour，源头是拉丁语 flos「花」，指植物上开放的那一部分。

senses.title: A plant grown for its flowers
senses.definition: a plant that is grown for its flowers
senses.definitionCN: 为了看花而栽种的植物
senses.example: She grows flowers along the garden wall.
senses.why: People speak of the whole plant by its brightest part, so flower also means the flowering plant in a garden.
senses.whyCN: 人们常拿一株植物最显眼的部分来称呼整株，所以 flower 也指园子里种的花卉。

senses.title: The finest part or prime
senses.definition: the best part of a group, or the time of greatest strength
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体里最好的部分，或力量最盛的时候
senses.example: He is in the flower of his youth.
senses.why: A flower is the fullest, brightest stage of a plant, so the word can name the best or most vigorous part of anything.
senses.whyCN: 花是一株植物最饱满、最明亮的阶段，所以这个词可以指任何事物最好、最盛的那部分。

senses.title: To produce flowers
senses.definition: to produce flowers, said of a plant
senses.definitionCN: 植物长出花朵
senses.example: The trees flower in May.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so flower describes a plant coming into bloom.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，flower 描述植物进入花期。

intro.en: The history of flower is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: flower 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Old French flour named the blossom of a plant.
items.cn: 古法语 flour 指植物的花朵。

items.en: The source is Latin flos, the word for a flower.
items.cn: 更早的来源是拉丁 flos「花」。

items.en: The word entered English as flour and then flower.
items.cn: 中古英语中它先作 flour，后作 flower。

items.en: It extended to the finest part of anything.
items.cn: 现代英语中扩展到事物的精华。
